title: No Frobenius-fixed vectors on the Tate module of an abelian variety
statement:
Let $A_0$ be an abelian variety over the finite field $k_0$ of [d-ab-field],
$A=A_0(\bar k)$, and $\ell\ne p$. Its rational Tate module has no nonzero
vector fixed by geometric Frobenius:

$$
(V_\ell A)^F=0.
$$

More precisely, with $T_\ell A$, $V_\ell A$ the Tate modules of the abelian
group $A$ ([def-tate-module-abelian-group]), on which the arithmetic
Frobenius $\sigma$ and $F=\sigma^{-1}$ act coordinatewise, one has
$(T_\ell A)^\sigma=(T_\ell A)^F=0$ and $(V_\ell A)^\sigma=(V_\ell A)^F=0$.

proof.text: The datum [d-ab-field] gives the automorphism $\sigma:z\mapsto z^q$ of $\bar k$ over $k_0$ and its coordinate action on $A=A_0(\bar k)$. Apply clause 3 of [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure] with $k=\bar k$ and $n=1$: $\{z\in\bar k:z^q=z\}=\iota(k_0)$, where $\iota:k_0\hookrightarrow\bar k$ is the structure embedding. Thus a value in $\bar k$ is fixed by $\sigma$ exactly when it comes from $k_0$.

source.place: first sentence: fixed field of the q-power Frobenius

proof.text: By the finite-type convention in [d-ab-field], choose a finite cover $U_j=\operatorname{Spec}R_j$ of $A_0$, with $R_j$ generated over $k_0$ by $m_j$ elements. A geometric point whose image lies in $U_j$ factors uniquely through this open chart (restrict its morphism and structure-sheaf map to the open). By the contravariant morphism correspondence of [def-weil-affine-spectrum], it is a $k_0$-algebra map $\varphi:R_j\to\bar k$. Precomposing its point map by $\operatorname{Spec}\sigma$ replaces $\varphi$ by $\sigma\circ\varphi$. Hence fixedness is exactly $\sigma\varphi(r)=\varphi(r)$ for every $r\in R_j$. By Step 1, such a map has a unique corestriction $\varphi_0:R_j\to k_0$, and conversely every $k_0$-algebra map to $k_0$ gives a fixed map after composing with $\iota$. A $k_0$-algebra map is determined by its values on the $m_j$ chosen generators: evaluate the same polynomial expression for any element of $R_j$. Its generator tuple has at most $q^{m_j}$ possibilities. Therefore the fixed geometric points landing in each $U_j$ form a finite set.

source.place: affine-chart paragraph: coordinate maps, corestriction and generator count

proof.text: Every geometric point lands in some $U_j$, since the field spectrum has one point [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The fixed set $A^\sigma$ is therefore contained in the union of the finitely many finite chart sets of Step 2, and is finite. The chart corestrictions also show $A^\sigma=A_0(k_0)$ inside $A_0(\bar k)$: extend the corestricted chart point along $U_j\hookrightarrow A_0$; conversely rational points have coordinates in $k_0$ and are fixed. No gluing of chart lifts is needed for the finiteness argument. In [d-ab-field], $A$ is an abelian group and $\sigma$ is a group automorphism, so its fixed set is a subgroup (it contains $0$ and is closed under subtraction).

source.place: conclusion of affine-chart paragraph: the fixed subgroup is finite

proof.text: Apply [lem-tate-module-no-fixed] to the abelian group $M=A$, the prime $\ell$ of [d-ab-field], and the coordinate automorphism $\sigma$. Its finite-fixed-subgroup hypothesis is Step 3. Its statement gives $(T_\ell A)^\sigma=0$ and $(V_\ell A)^\sigma=0$, and gives the same conclusions for $\sigma^{-1}=F$. The actions are exactly the coordinatewise action and its extension to fractions specified in [def-tate-module-abelian-group], so these are all four asserted vanishings, including $(V_\ell A)^F=0$.

source.place: last sentence: apply the finite-fixed-subgroup Tate-module lemma
